A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reflection-removal system and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–G. Content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, PSNR/SSIM comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and results on captured photographs in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds simulation ablations, additional comparator results, and failure and 8-bit-input examples.

M1.justification: The RAW simulation, base architecture, upsampler, and losses remain unchanged. Section F.2 and Figure S13 add a limited inference adaptation: pseudo-inverting gamma before applying the RAW-trained model to 8-bit photographs.

E1.justification: MIT5K, RAISE, Laval Indoors, and the established real-photo scenarios remain. Figure S13 extends testing to finished 8-bit inputs for the RAW-trained model. The public benchmarks newly listed in Section 5.2 are discussed as unsuitable, not actually evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds Zhu as an evaluated base-model comparator under RAW retraining and published 8-bit weights; v2 only cited that work. The ground-truth upsampling comparison expands beyond V-DESIRR to bicubic, SUPIR, and Real-ESRGAN, labeled RESRGan in Table 3.

E3.justification: v3 introduces training on ablated simulation datasets of approximately 1.2M examples each, evaluation on the full-simulation test set, and published-weight evaluation on an Adobe Camera RAW-converted 8-bit test set. Tables 1–2 add control-relative SSIM improvement measures. Section 5.1 also changes the stated test allocation from 15% to 5%, assigning 15% to validation, while retaining sample counts; this establishes a reporting change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 1 tests gamma compression, exposure, pose, Fresnel attenuation, white balance, blur/double reflection, and combined omissions. Figures S12–S13 add failure examples and RAW-versus-8-bit robustness analysis. Existing context and upsampler ablations remain, but v2's qualitative observation that constant context produces unreliable performance is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions use selected p-value thresholds and qualitative significance statements without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical-test procedures. v3 extends this practice to new ablations; additional significance outcomes and the changed p-value attribution concern results rather than a new statistical methodology.

E6.justification: Existing matched base-model and upsampler scores remain unchanged after SSIM percentage rescaling. v3 adds simulation-ablation scores, Zhu and published 8-bit results, three upsampling comparator rows, and failure/8-bit examples. For example, new All+G results give SSIMt 89.2% versus 95.7% for full simulation. The ours-versus-ours+rnd passage also replaces a nonsignificance statement with p < 1.7e-11 despite unchanged scores.

T1.justification: The photometric equations, Fresnel formulas, defocus derivation, double-reflection assumptions, contextual geometry, and loss definitions are retained. Equation renumbering and notation changes do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion add a central claim that RAW simulation training improves performance more than architectural differences among prior methods. v2 claimed generalization from synthetic data and benefits from RAW, context, and full-resolution processing, but did not make this comparative claim about their relative importance.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit qualifications concerning 8-bit camera-processing differences, missed lights and halos, and the preference for glass covering the field of view. It also discusses privacy implications of recovering hidden reflections. Existing explanations of saturation, overlapping textures, nighttime failures, and upsampling errors largely remain.

D1.justification: Section F.2 newly specifies image precision, including stated ≥15-bit field photographs, uint16 processing, and 12-/14-bit source proportions of 43%/57%. Architecture details, loss weights, hardware, and DNG SDK pseudocode remain. v2's explicit statement that rectangular-image tiles are linearly blended is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds Real-ESRGAN and SUPIR references and removes the contextual-loss and LPIPS citations, although LPIPS remains in the loss specification. The related-work categories largely persist, with stronger positioning of RAW-based training relative to architectural variations.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively condensed and rewritten, especially the introduction, method summaries, and results narrative. The detailed ACR-path explanation moves into a footnote, and the supplement gains a contents guide. The overall section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Architecture Figures 2–3 move to supplementary Figures S4–S5, while a system overview is added. Tables are expanded and reorganized, and new simulation-overview, failure, and 8-bit figures appear. Existing image panels are rearranged, enlarged or reduced, and some faces are blurred.

improvement.justification: v3 adds controlled simulation ablations where v2 relied on qualitative motivation, while broader comparisons and explicit failure/8-bit limitations improve support and transparency. The gain is limited by the new RAW-versus-architecture claim: its approximately 40-point improvement concerns control-relative percentages, while training and input conditions also differ. The changed split description and inconsistent p-value attribution further reduce reporting clarity.
